correctness.rationale: I independently reconstructed the complex from the degree-at-most-two definition. It has 1081 faces including the empty face and f-vector \((12,66,204,360,324,114)\). Replaying the stated toggle order leaves exactly 539 matched pairs and two critical nonempty faces: one vertex and one six-edge simplex. I independently oriented all 4488 nonempty Hasse covers according to the Morse matching and topologically sorted all 1080 nonempty faces, confirming acyclicity. Hence Forman theory gives a CW model with one 0-cell and one 5-cell and no intervening cells; the unique 5-cell attaches to a point, giving \(S^5\). The repository verifier additionally contains an independent mod-two boundary-rank check.

originality.rationale: Singh's full primary paper gives exact homotopy types for the shellable range \(m>r\ge n\) and for the balanced boundary \(M_{n-1}(K_{n,n})\). After ordering \(K_{3,4}\) as \(K_{4,3}\), the audited case has \(r=2<n=3\), so neither theorem applies. The same paper notes Reiner--Roberts rational homology formulas for broad higher chessboard complexes, but rational homology does not imply the homotopy-sphere statement. Resultary search returned the assigned finding and other graph-complex computations, not a prior \(K_{3,4}\) homotopy theorem.

value.rationale: This is the first unequal complete-bipartite case immediately outside Singh's exact regimes and a natural small boundary in higher matching complexes. An exact homotopy type, certified by a complete Morse matching rather than only homology, is a useful structural benchmark.

final_claim: The two-matching complex \(M_2(K_{3,4})\) is homotopy equivalent to \(S^5\).
limitations: This is an exact finite computation for \(K_{3,4}\); it does not classify \(M_2(K_{3,n})\) for larger \(n\) or the whole unresolved region \(r<\min(m,n)\).
